## What's new

- **r2backup lives in the Windows taskbar.** The installer adds
  **r2backup** to the Start menu and offers to start it. An icon next to
  the clock is green when your backups are fine, blue while one runs and
  red when a folder needs a look; a click opens a panel with each
  folder's last backup, live progress, and **Back up now**. Everything
  that used to need a terminal is in it: connecting storage, adding a
  folder and choosing what it includes, automatic backups, restoring
  files, recovering deleted ones, and usage and cost.

- **Back up to Drime.** Drime is now a second place to keep backups,
  alongside Cloudflare R2. It needs one API token. Backups appear as
  ordinary folders under **r2backup** in your Drime, so you can browse
  and download them from the Drime web app without r2backup at all.

- **A second copy, with another company.** Keep a copy of your backups
  on R2 if they go to Drime, or the other way round, and have it updated
  after every backup. In the panel it is **Settings → Account → Second
  copy**; in the terminal, `r2b mirror`.

- **Sign in with your email, no password.** The panel asks for an email
  and sends a 6-digit code. Your storage keys are kept with your account,
  so another computer signed in with the same email gets them without
  typing them again.

- **Every backup in one place.** The clock icon in the panel lists every
  backup in your storage, grouped by computer. Open one to restore from
  it, or delete one no folder uses any more.

- **Name your computer.** Under **Settings → Account → Computers**, the
  pencil next to this computer renames it. New folders are filed under
  the new name; folders already backed up stay where they are.

- **Deleting asks where.** With a second copy, deleting a backup asks
  whether to delete it from both places or only from where backups go.

## Fixed

- **A deleted folder's backup stayed on the second copy forever.** It
  now goes from both when you say so, and stays on the second copy when
  you choose "only here".

## Heads up

- On Windows 10 the taskbar app needs the
  [WebView2 Runtime](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703)
  (Windows 11 has it). If it is missing, the app says so when it starts.
